subject: Geography
description: Parallels, meridians, important lines, time zones

questions.stem: The imaginary line that divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres is called the:
questions.explanation: The Equator (latitude 0°) is the great circle equidistant from the poles — divides Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres. The Prime Meridian (longitude 0°, through Greenwich) divides East and West Hemispheres. Other key parallels — Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N), Tropic of Capricorn (23.5° S), Arctic Circle (66.5° N), Antarctic Circle (66.5° S).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The 'Tropic of Cancer' passes through how many Indian states?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N) passes through eight Indian states — from west to east — Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram. A popular mnemonic: 'Go Race Mom Cha-Cha Ju Who-a Tells Mi' or simply memorise the order west-to-east: Gu-Ra-MP-CG-JH-WB-TR-MZ.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Indian Standard Time (IST) is based on the 82.5° E longitude, which passes through:
questions.explanation: IST is GMT+5:30 — derived from longitude 82.5° E (since 15° of longitude = 1 hour; 82.5 × 4 min/° = 330 min = 5:30 hours). The 82.5° E meridian passes through Mirzapur (UP) and is called the Standard Meridian of India. It also passes through AP and parts of Odisha. Only ONE time zone for the whole country; debated periodically (NE states lose early daylight).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The difference in time between Gujarat (westernmost India) and Arunachal Pradesh (easternmost India) is approximately:
questions.explanation: India spans longitudes ~68° E (Gujarat) to ~97° E (Arunachal Pradesh) — about 29° of longitude. Time difference = 29° × 4 min/° ≈ 116 min ≈ ~2 hours. Because India uses a single IST, 'sunrise' in Arunachal is nearly 2 hours before Gujarat. This is why debates on dual-time-zones (IST-1 for NE, IST for the rest) keep recurring.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: A point at latitude 0°, longitude 0° would be located in:
questions.explanation: The intersection of 0° latitude (Equator) and 0° longitude (Prime Meridian) lies in the Gulf of Guinea, off the west coast of Africa — roughly south of Ghana. There's no land at exactly this point. The nearest named location is 'Null Island' — a virtual landmark popular in GIS / navigation datasets when something 'falls through' coordinate checks.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Each degree of longitude corresponds to a time difference of:
questions.explanation: Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours → 360°/24 = 15° per hour → 15°/60 min = 1° per 4 minutes. So every 1° of longitude eastward adds 4 minutes to local time (and westward subtracts 4 minutes). 15° difference = 1 hour — the basis of standard time zones. Knowing this converts any longitude difference to a time difference.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The southernmost point of the Indian mainland is:
questions.explanation: Kanyakumari (Cape Comorin) at ~8°4′ N is the southernmost tip of the Indian MAINLAND. The southernmost point of Indian TERRITORY is Indira Point on Great Nicobar Island (~6°45′ N). Indira Point was partially submerged by the 2004 tsunami. The northernmost point is Indira Col in the Siachen / Karakoram area.
